label: Kyriba claim boundary
query: If Kyriba is not live yet, what exactly can Lakeshore claim today without overstating value?
answer: My read For Lakeshore Holdings, you can safely claim Kyriba as a well-advanced, stage-backed treasury selection program with complete sourcing and strategy artifacts — but you should not claim realized business value, live production benefits, or completed transition/implementation yet. Why 1) Program spine status is explicit: for LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026, Strategy through BAFO are approved; Executive Decision, Selection, Transition, and Value are still in review/needs-review states. That means you have a fully documented evaluation and negotiated position, not a finished go-live. 2) The Source spine is retrievable: you can say “we have a complete Kyriba Source artifact spine” — strategy, requirements, evaluation, commercial terms, and BAFO are grounded and can be surfaced as evidence. 3) No production signals yet: there is no indication in the current tenant substrate of a completed decision gate, cutover plan in execution, or live runtime telemetry — so any “value” language must be future-oriented or scenario-based, not realized. Concrete claim boundary you can use today You can say: Lakeshore has completed a structured, evidence-backed Kyriba treasury RFP and BAFO (LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026), with full artifacts retrievable in Source. Strategy, requirements, vendor evaluation, and BAFO are approved and form the basis for executive decision and implementation planning. Expected value is quantified in the strategy/BAFO artifacts, but realization will depend on the forthcoming Executive Decision and Transition phases. What you should avoid stating as of now “Kyriba is live in production at Lakeshore” — not supported.Evidence checked: intake.tenant_context (loaded tenant context), telemetry.value_attestation (verified versus projected value), intake.missing_fields (missing or stale evidence fields), intake.question_scope (question scope).
